title: Seed the auth module's permission keys so tenant administrators can open the audit pages
goal: Tenant Smoke has been red on every commit since the tenant console remediation merged. A provisioned tenant administrator reaches /system/login-log and /system/security-event, sees them in the sidebar, and gets '403 no permission' from the route guard. Navigation is resolved from system_role_menu, but authorisation is resolved from system_role_permission, and the auth module's menu seeder (SeedAuthModuleMenus) only ever wrote the menu half. The system module's seeder writes both halves, so the twelve audit keys (system:login-log:*, system:session:*, system:security-event:*) were missing from the platform administrator itself; tenant provisioning copies that key set, so every tenant administrator inherited the same hole. This task adds a shared idempotent grant primitive, makes both seeders use it, and pins the copy behaviour with tests that run against real MySQL.
findings: P0: SeedAuthModuleMenus (backend/modules/auth/login/login_menu.go) bound the menu and system_role_menu but never wrote system_role_permission, so the login-log, session and security-event pages were navigable and unauthorised at the same time.

P0: because tenant provisioning copies the platform administrator's key set, the twelve missing keys were missing for every tenant administrator — the visible failure was a tenant-side 403 with a platform-side cause.
P1: the platform administrator's key set in CI held 85 keys; the twelve audit keys were absent, which also broke those pages for the platform console itself.
P1: the test fixtures declared system_role_permission without tenant_id, so the old seeder (which omitted tenant_id) passed and the divergence from the production table went unnoticed.

P2: two independent implementations of 'grant one permission key to the platform administrator' existed (seed.go's ensureAdminPermissionSeed and nothing in the auth module), inviting exactly this kind of drift.

in: backend/modules/auth/login/login_menu.go (seed PagePerm and Perms after binding the menu)
out: Changing the system_role_permission or system_role_menu schema or migrations
Adding a tenant dimension to system_menu
Automatically re-granting keys to already-provisioned tenants (a tenant may have revoked them deliberately)
Extending requiredAPIRoutesByPermission with the login-log and session routes

implementationNotes: The fix belongs upstream. provisionTenantRoleBindings is correct by design (copy the platform administrator's key set, confine by tenant domain); patching the tenant's key set would leave the platform console broken and the next tenant broken again.

EnsureRolePermission writes tenant_id explicitly. The login permission loader filters on system_role_permission.tenant_id = <login tenant>, so a grant written without it lands in tenant 0 and a tenant subject never sees the key — the same trap already documented on insertRoleMenuSQL.
The two menu seeders are not merged: they own different menu data (keys, parents, ordering). Only the write primitive is shared, through pkg/rbacbind.
The fixtures now mirror the production table. The old fixture had no tenant_id column, which is precisely why a seeder that omitted tenant_id could look correct for so long.
tenant_member stays read-only: isReadOnlyPermissionKey is unchanged, so the member role receives only :list/:detail/:view/:tree/:export keys.

commands: cd backend && go build ./... && go vet ./...
npm run check:task-packet && npm run check:docs-frontmatter && npm run check:structure
runtimeEvidence: CI backend log for the failing run: INSERT INTO system_role_permission rows for tenant 204 role 4 number 85 and contain no system:login-log:*, system:security-event:* or system:session:* key
go test ./modules/system/iam/tenant/ -run TestProvisionTenant_CopiesPlatformAdminPermissionKeys proves the copy path end to end against real MySQL
go test ./modules/auth/login/ -run TestSeedAuthModuleMenusGrantsAdminPermissionKeys proves the platform administrator now holds all twelve keys and that re-seeding does not duplicate them
The Playwright assertion itself can only be produced by CI: this machine cannot spawn a browser (spawnSync EBUSY)

humanGates: Whether existing tenants must be re-provisioned on upgrade, or given an operator-facing backfill command, is a maintainer decision. This packet does not auto-backfill: a tenant administrator may have revoked keys deliberately.
Whether the login-log and session routes should be added to requiredAPIRoutesByPermission (the permission workbench remediation table) is a product decision and is out of scope here.
